logical_structure.title: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: View PDF
The activities at this stage must be carefully managed to support the Principles of Procurement.
As a minimum processes must be undertaken in a transparent manner, ensuring no market place distortion.
The procurement process cannot unduly favour or disadvantage a supplier. It is your responsibility to ensure these requirements are met.
Access to the ITT and any related documents should be non-discriminatory, generally available and free of charge.
Quickfire Guide
Invitation to Tender Document Contents
A quickfire guide for the sections you should include in your ITT, where relevant to your procurement.
Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: When using a two stage process, documents will only be made available to bidders who have passed the selection stage. Invitations to submit a tender should be issued simultaneously to all bidders and in writing.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: If you are not using a separate selection stage, ITTs should be issued on request to any interested supplier. This can be at any point prior to the tender submission date set.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Where ITT documents cannot be issued electronically (for example because the information is sensitive or the contract is of a nature that requires specialised tools and/or files) then you can use other means to issue the documents. If you do this, it would be good practice to increase the tender time limit by five working days to allow for this extra process.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Evaluation Criteria, including Financial Criteria
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: The evaluation criteria and weightings must be published within the Contract Notice. For more information refer to Selection, Award & Exclusion .
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Price/financial evaluation criteria should include:
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Whole Life Cost comparisons
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Quantifiable financial benefits arising from the technical evaluation (e.g. speed, fuel or electricity consumption, coverage, shelf life, etc.)
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Fixed or variable pricing
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Cost of components, spare parts, consumables and servicing
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Life-cycle costing where appropriate.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Risk analysis and financial appraisal (for major contracts of strategic importance, especially those of an innovative nature).
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: To support this process, as you are developing the documentation you will draw information from the Develop Strategy stage of the Procurement Journey.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: It is best practice to agree the evaluation criteria with the User Intelligence Group (UIG). These criteria will identify which eligible tenderer(s) will deliver best value for money for the organisation, based on the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT).
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: You should identify the Most Economically Advantageous Tender, assessed on the criteria linked to the contract's subject matter. This should include price or cost evaluation using a cost effectiveness approach. A cost effectiveness approach may include Life Cycle Impact Mapping
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: It is important to differentiate between Whole Life Costing and Life Cycle Costing and further information on both an be found in Additional Resources.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Lifecycle Impact Mapping
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Focuses on social and environmental impact rather than cost.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Life-cycle impact mapping helps you identify and assess impacts. For example, you may focus attention on the disposal phase before beginning the procurement. This then allows you to build end-of-life management requirements into performance clauses and internal management procedures.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Please note: Life-cycle impact mapping can be used alongside life-cycle costing as part of the procurement process.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Other considerations for ITT documentation
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: You may wish to consider the areas below for inclusion within the ITT documentation:
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: e-Commerce: e-Capability, e-Procurement Information, e-Auctions, etc.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Contract implementation/contract and supplier management information
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Proposed implementation plan
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Management information - requirement to provide line item detail
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Roles & Responsibilities
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Mini-competition guidance: details of process to be followed for call offs
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Invitation to Tender
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: The ITT or the Invitation to Confirm Interest should include comprehensive information for potential bidders about the requirement being tendered. While there are a number of Generic Documents listed below that will require insertion into all packs (e.g. a reference to the relevant Contract Notice or Award Criteria weightings) some of the content will naturally be specific to each requirement and you should select those that you need to include in the ITT pack from the list below:
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: A reference to the relevant Contract Notice, previously published
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Instructions to bidders including the tender submission deadline; address to which the tender submission is to be sent and the language which the tender submission must be submitted in
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: It is good practice to issue an SPD to bidders. For more information, please refer to Selection Criteria and SPD
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Award Criteria weightings
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: For services contracts, if deemed applicable, you should ask the bidders to indicate any share of the contract that the tenderer may subcontract and information about the subcontractors including their name and contact details. You may request separate SPD responses from subcontractors and consortium members, when deemed appropriate, in order to safeguard the effective delivery of the contract, based on relevance and proportionality to the contract
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: For contracts which may be extended, the nature, quantity and, where possible, the estimated time for exercising options
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: For supply or service contracts, the nature, quantity and, where possible, estimated publication dates of notices of future tenders
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: If applicable to the contract, the delivery of supplies commencement or termination date(s)
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: The address of the Organisation who will award the contract
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Economic and technical conditions, financial guarantees and any information required from bidders
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: The form of the contract to be used e.g. purchase, lease, hire-purchase, or a combination
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: If electronic access to the relevant Procurement Documents cannot be offered the address and deadline date for requesting Procurement Documents and the language(s) to be used
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Background and overview of the tendering and evaluation process including details of presentations and site visits, if applicable
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Terms and Conditions which will apply to any resulting contract with the principle supplier
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Specification and technical requirements
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Sustainable Procurement Duty requirements e.g. economic, social and environmental considerations including community benefits and Fair Work Practices. See Sustainable Procurement Tools
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Cyber Security Requirements (example ITT and Contract Notice wording when using the Cyber Security Procurement Support Tool )
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: Quality questionnaire
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents

content_blocks.text: The activities at this stage must be carried out in a carefully managed manner that support the Principles of Procurement . It is the responsibility of you and your Organisation to make sure these requirements are met.
heading_path: Availability of Invitation to Tender Documents
